programme.title: Bill Paterson Remembers - The Cheviot, The Stag and The Black, Black Oil

Bill's involvement with the production began when he was a young member of the left wing theatre company '7:84' - so named to reflect their claim that seven percent of the population owned 84 percent of the UK's wealth - and saw him originally playing not one but two roles, as Glasgow property speculator McChuckemup and the oilman known as 'Texas Bill'

programme.desc: Behind the scenes on Princess Cruises and Regent Seven Seas Cruises, following staff as they experience the highs and lows of working life at sea. From demanding shifts and missing home to late-night camaraderie and off-duty adventures. The newest ship in the Princess Cruises fleet - the Star Princess - sets sail from Fort Lauderdale on a month-long voyage around the Caribbean. It's turnaround day, and guest services manager Magda and her assistant Lewis are racing to check in thousands of new guests, including cruising virgins Ross and Vishal from Edinburgh, who are celebrating 10 years together, and teenagers Harry and Sonny from Worcestershire, who are marking Harry's 18th birthday. On the bridge, commodore Nick Nash from Cornwall needs 90% of guests to complete their safety checks before he can cast off, and with the clock ticking, it's cutting things fine. Once at sea, the ship's young dancers and singers throw themselves into giving guests a taste of the entertainment in store. The next morning brings paradise itself: white sand and turquoise water at Princess Cays in the Bahamas, where non-swimmer Vishal is coaxed onto a paddleboard by his husband Ross. As the sun goes down, the ship's formal night gets underway, complete with a 280-glass champagne waterfall, and Harry's mum Wendy has a magical birthday surprise up her sleeve

From demanding shifts and missing home to late-night camaraderie and off-duty adventures. The newest ship in the Princess Cruises fleet - the Star Princess - sets sail from Fort Lauderdale on a month-long voyage around the Caribbean. It's turnaround day, and guest services manager Magda and her assistant Lewis are racing to check in thousands of new guests, including cruising virgins Ross and Vishal from Edinburgh, who are celebrating 10 years together, and teenagers Harry and Sonny from Worcestershire, who are marking Harry's 18th birthday. On the bridge, commodore Nick Nash from Cornwall needs 90% of guests to complete their safety checks before he can cast off, and with the clock ticking, it's cutting things fine. Once at sea, the ship's young dancers and singers throw themselves into giving guests a taste of the entertainment in store. The next morning brings paradise itself: white sand and turquoise water at Princess Cays in the Bahamas, where non-swimmer Vishal is coaxed onto a paddleboard by his husband Ross. As the sun goes down, the ship's formal night gets underway, complete with a 280-glass champagne waterfall, and Harry's mum Wendy has a magical birthday surprise up her sleeve

programme.title: Wild Animal Babies
programme.desc: For animals born in bulk, life is a battle from the very start. Patrick Aryee marvels at the strategies nature has come up with to raise the next generation

programme.title: David Attenborough Meets Obama
programme.desc: Another chance to see Barack Obama's conversation, recorded in May 2015, with renowned naturalist and film-maker David Attenborough. In a twist on usual convention, the then-US president took the role of interviewer, quizzing Attenborough about his thoughts on the future of the planet, their shared passion for nature, and potential ways to protect the environment. Also includes behind-the-scenes footage from Sir David's latest project on the Great Barrier Reef, as well as highlights from throughout the veteran broadcaster's career

programme.title: Flying Monsters with David Attenborough
programme.desc: The broadcaster explores the world of the pterosaur, a flying creature that occupied the skies 200 million years ago. Visiting sites around the world, from the Dorset coast to New Mexico, he explains how the reptiles evolved to defy the forces of gravity, and examines the features of their anatomy that can still be seen in present-day descendents. He also discovers why they became extinct after dominating the skies for millions of years

programme.title: David Attenborough's Natural History Museum Alive
programme.desc: The broadcaster invites viewers to join him as he takes an after-hours stroll around one of his favourite places, the Natural History Museum. But this is no ordinary tour as some of the many exhibits spring to life as the veteran naturalist strolls along

programme.title: Deadly Australians
programme.desc: From the oceans and the forest to swamps and deserts, a look at the toxic, venomous and dangerous creatures that Australia is home to

programme.title: Wolves and Lions: Old Enemies
programme.desc: A look at how canids and felines deploy an arsenal of hunting skills. Felines rely on endurance, and wolves on their privileged sense of smell in a fight for survival

programme.title: Land of the Far North
programme.desc: Life in the Arctic Circle, where the sun hardly sets in summer. Food is abundant, but animals and plants alike face great challenges such as sleep deprivation, pests and predators

programme.title: Land of the Far North
programme.desc: Cold and darkness dominate the Arctic Circle during winter, but nature copes astonishingly well. This documentary reveals how plants and animals survive these brutal conditions

programme.title: Wild Philippines
programme.desc: Cameras follow turtles and tiger sharks roaming volcanic reefs, and tarsiers leaping through forests on the hunt

programme.title: Wolves and Lions: Old Enemies

programme.title: Wild Castles

programme.title: Osprey

programme.title: Great Lakes Wild

programme.title: Great Lakes Wild
programme.desc: A dam is an engineering feat that controls massive amounts of water. But as this episode shows, it can also wreak havoc on the animals that call those waters home

programme.title: Mysteries of Evolution
programme.desc: The importance of cooperation in the animal kingdom, where some creatures work together to be social while others put the welfare of the group above their own potential

programme.title: Mysteries of Evolution
programme.desc: From the shark to the horseshoe crab, meet the planet's 'living fossils' - the creatures that have survived relatively unchanged for millions of years

programme.title: How the Wild Things Sleep

programme.title: Animals at Play
programme.desc: Part one of two. The reasons why young animals enjoy playing, and how it can teach them to survive in the wild. The programme explores how young elephants, which rarely leave their mothers' side for the first eight years of life, play to develop social skills, while macaques hone their mental agility by playing games with stones. Plus, a zoologist who looks after orphaned cheetahs reveals how play can help cubs learn to hunt

programme.title: Animals at Play
programme.desc: Part two of two. The secrets behind animals' group games, from dolphins that play catch to a hyena tug of war, revealing the benefits they gain from their playful behaviour. The programme examines how breaching the rules of a game can have fatal consequences - but how it also presents an opportunity for animals with a rigid hierarchy to break down social barriers

In Australia, meet the world's most venomous snake, and in nearby oceans, discover the deadly nature of the marine creatures that share these tropical waters

programme.title: World's Most Toxic Animals

programme.title: Bears of the Karawank Mountains

programme.title: David Attenborough's First Life
programme.desc: In the first of a two-part documentary, the naturalist explores the origins of life on Earth. Beginning the journey near his childhood home in Charnwood Forest, Leicestershire, he learns how a fossil discovery transformed scientists' understanding of the evolution of complex organisms, and in Newfoundland and Australia he reveals the earliest kinds of animal to exist on the planet. With the help of cutting-edge technology and visual effects, the programme brings the creatures to life, demonstrating how they survived

programme.title: David Attenborough's First Life

programme.title: Life
programme.desc: David Attenborough turns his attention to marine invertebrates - bizarre and beautiful animals that thrive in the toughest parts of the ocean. Divers swim into a shoal of predatory Humboldt squid emerging from the depths to hunt in packs, and timelapse photography reveals starfish gathering under the Arctic ice to devour a seal carcass. programme.title: Life
programme.desc: The strategies adopted by plants that enable them to grow in every possible environment, even where there is no sunlight, water or nutrients. Featuring the dragon's blood tree, which survives in the desert by converting moisture found in the mist and shading its own roots, the carnivorous Venus flytrap that has evolved into an extraordinary predator able to digest insects, and the cat's claw creeper, which uses other plants as a ladder to reach sunlight. Narrated by David Attenborough

programme.title: Life
